title: Boerne Little League returns home to parade after Little League World Series appearance
text:
The Boerne Little League baseball team returned home to the Lone Star State around 3 p.m. Wednesday, and the community showed the boys it has their support — win or lose.
The team was one of only 10 teams representing the US at the Little League World Series. Overall, they were one of 20 teams from around the world to make it to this stage.
– The Boerne Little League baseball team returned home to the Lone Star State around 3 p.m. Wednesday, and the community showed the boys it has their support — win or lose. Police and first responders escorted the team before the community welcomed them with a parade. Afterward, the players stuck around to take pictures and sign autographs.
“It was extremely special to watch them fully commit to achieving their goal. Day in, day out, making sacrifices, not having a summer vacation, time away from family and friends,” said Rusty Belden, one of the Boerne Little League baseball assistant coaches.
“They just worked their tails off. ” The team was one of only 10 teams representing the United States at the Little League World Series. Overall, they were one of 20 teams from around the world to reach that stage.
“My favorite memories were just meeting the other teams and meeting other MLB players,” said Walker Yost, a Boerne Little League baseball player. Ashley Gonzalez Ashley Gonzalez is a sports reporter at KSAT. She joined the team from Jacksonville, Florida, where she was the weekend sports anchor. Before her time in Jacksonville, she was in Corpus Christi at KIII.
There, she became the first woman sports anchor in the station's history.
